sections.html: At present three species of the genus Tetranematichthys are distinguished. They reach about 20 cm total length. They feed predatorily, the preferred food being small fish.
• IUCN Red List: Least Concern (IUCN 2023). The species is widely distributed and faces no direct threats.

None of the Tetranematichthys species comes frequently or even regularly into the trade, because their hidden way of life makes their catch a pure matter of luck. T. wallacei was imported from Colombia, and the import included sexually mature males and females.

T. wallacei differs from the identically colored species T. quadrifilis by the profile of the underside of the head. The cheeks of T. wallacei run almost parallel on the left and right side, while in T. quadrifilis the distance between left and right head edge increases clearly recognizable towards the abdomen.
South America: Amazon basin: upper Negro River system in Brazil and Venezuela and upper Orinoco River basin in southern Venezuela.

A tank for Tetranematichthys should contain fine sand on the bottom, should be softly lit and should be equipped with a great number of driftwood. During daytime the fish often sleep lying on the side. This behaviour is absolutely normal and no reason for the aquarist to become anxious.

An aquarium for Tetranematichthys should contain a fine sandy bottom, be dimly lit and contain plenty of root wood for hiding.
They feed predatorily, preferred food being small fish.

It is carnivorous and prefers to feed on small fish. Prefers live foods given at lights out. Try different choices of frozen foods to see what they prefer as they can be picky in their dietary requirements.
During the day the animals often lie on their sides sleeping; this is quite normal and need not worry the keeper. Among themselves Tetranematichthys are completely peaceful.
The males develop an extended dorsal fin and is thorny.

As in the closely related genus Ageinosus, male Tetranematichthys develop a huge dorsal fin at breeding time. After the reproductive period, both sexual characteristics are said to regress and then become almost indistinguishable from that of the female.
The male uses the heavily spined dorsal fin spine to clamp the female during mating. Fertilization occurs internally with a penis-like structure formed from the anteriormost rays of the anal fin.
Lexicon: Tetranematichthys means "fish with four filaments", referring to the barbels. wallacei: dedication name for Alfred Russel Wallace (1823-1913).

Description: Distinguished from T. quadrifilis in the alignment of the lateral margins of the head in the region from the anterior margin of the orbit to the posterior limit of the opercle (running approximately in parallel from ventral view vs. diverging laterally, respectively); in the body width at the pectoral-fin insertion as a proportion of the head width at the posterior margin of the orbit (0.99-1.10 vs. 1.17-1.25, respectively); in the distance from the tip of the snout to the anal fin origin (0.29-0.32 of SL vs. 0.33-0.36 of SL, respectively); and in the position of the anterior termination of the gill opening (one orbital diameter posterior of the transverse plane running through the posterior margin of the orbit vs. positioned in the transverse plane running through the center of the orbit, respectively).

Etymology: The genus name Tetranematichthys means "fish with four threats"; this refers to the barbels. The specific name wallacei: named after Alfred Russel Wallace when, starting in 1848, made large collections of plants and animals in the Amazon basin.
